definition: A sitting of the Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament used in this archive as a hard competition-maths benchmark alongside AIME, on the order of 30 problems. It appears mainly in parallel-reasoning and test-time-scaling evaluations, where sources use it as the case that breaks an aggregate: it is named as the one regression in a method that gains elsewhere, and as the ablation set where removing a component costs the most. At that size a few items move the score by several points, so per-benchmark differences here are not separable from noise without repeated runs.

evidence.note: CLR reallocates part of the test-time compute budget from generating more solution samples to falsifying a small set of decision-critical claims extracted from each trace, improving accuracy over self-consistency while using fewer tokens on some models.
evidence.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

evidence.note: Introduces OptimalThinkingBench, a unified benchmark pairing OverthinkingBench (simple queries) and UnderthinkingBench (hard reasoning/math) with a shared F1 metric, showing that none of 33 evaluated LLMs balances accuracy and thinking-token efficiency.
evidence.title: OptimalThinkingBench: Evaluating Over and Underthinking in LLMs

name: HMMT25
